A purposive random sampling technique was used to select
150 pre-service teachers (300 and 400 level) from five departments in
the Faculty of Education at the University of Ibadan offering
economics. A convenience sampling technique was used to sample 10
students for focus group discussions, who served as team leaders in
service-learning courses. The Students’ Prosocial and Professional
Competencies Questio

A validated questionnaire was used to assess prosocial abilities, which included the subconstructs of communication,
teamwork, empathy, cultural competency, and social responsibility skills (r = 0.79), with a reliability coefficient
established using Cronbach’s alpha. The study adhered to ethical considerations, providing comprehensive information
about its objectives, methodol

The study was conducted over six months, from March 20, 2024, to September 27, 2024. The instruments were
administered at a convenient time for the participants. The FGD was conducted in two sessions, each lasting 45 minutes,
approximately 90 minutes. Quantitative data collected were analyzed using mean, standard deviation and paired
sample t-test at a significant level of 0.05, while the qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis, identifying
major themes and patterns related to the influence of service-learning on participants’ prosocial competencies and
employability.
Results and Findings

This study provides empirical evidence
supporting the effectiveness of service learning on graduate employability, suggesting that teacher education programs in
Nigeria and beyond should consider incorporating service learning components to enhance graduate outcomes. These
improvements not only prepare employees for the complexities of the classroom but also make them more competitive
and attracti

Despite a positive trend in empathy gains among the
pre-service teachers, the study’s results showed limited statistical significance. This implies that while the intervention
might have influenced the participants’ empathetic responses, we should interpret the changes observed cautiously.
Likewise, the generalizability of the results is constrained by contextual factors such as sample size, demographic
characteristics, and the specific setting of the study.

I found this paper to be highly valuable for other researchers and even those in charge of
planning and developing curriculum for teacher educators. However, there is need to pay
attention to few method and analytical approaches in the paper to ensure clarity and applicability
of its findings.
In the abstract under the background, the word "unprepared" seems inappropriate. It is the
degree that supposed to prepare them, not the workforce. It could read: "Many graduates are
discouraged about the labor market...." The statement should be reviewed in first paragraph of
the introduction. It seems that the student selected for the focus group discussion were selected
because of their position during the course. It might be more purposive instead of convenient,
except there are many of them, from which 10 were selected as they are available.
The authors should check some typographical errors in the manuscript, such as paragraph
sentence five in paragraph six of the introduction.
I don't think it is necessary to have a title on a single paragraph: Service-learning in teacher
education.
Is the description of the sample not too narrow for easy identification? You do not need to
mention the university.
Was there a factor analysis that showed five factors? The reliability reported is the overall I
suppose.
If you use some software for both quantitative and qualitative analysis they could be mentioned
under methods even if there are no citations for them.
